How do you think default moderators should be regulated on voat?

I don't think they should be regulated, or at least not beyond whatever the actual owners of the site might choose to do, and I think that they should be very sparing in their intervention.

Too much intervention is exactly what destroyed Reddit.

Reddit has had abusive mods for YEARS. All that meant was that the mods ruined individual subs, and all that meant was that users who wanted to avoid those mods just moved to different subs. And it worked. Or, more accurately, it worked UNTIL the admin stepped in and institutionalized one set of "acceptable" viewpoints and empowered mods to enforce that particular set of viewpoints. That was exactly the point at which a problem that had formerly been limited to individual subs became site-wide.

Any mechanism that would serve to "regulate" mods would place sufficient authority in the hands of a few to control content site-wide, and any such authority WILL, sooner or later, be captured by the most noxious of authoritarian assholes, since they're the ones who want it most and they're the ones who are most willing to go to whatever lengths are necessary to gain it and hold it.

Exactly as they've done on Reddit, and on Wikipedia, and so on.

As they say, power corrupts. And the more power there is, the more corruption there will be. Each time you try to curb corruption by adding another layer of power above it to "regulate" it, all you end up doing is creating a greater power that will, itself, be corrupted.

Yeah, the democratic features of content aggregators are unfortunately easy to game. I think developers need to invent measures to prevent users from gaming the system.

But, I think holding default moderators accountable to the userbase is necessary. The problem with reddit is that moderators were inevitably accountable only to the administrators.

Do you think we should just allow censorship on default subs?

The problem with reddit is that moderators were inevitably accountable only to the administrators.

Moderators never harmed "Reddit." They didn't have (and still don't have) that sort of power. They only harmed individual subs - that's the extent of their authority, so it's all they ever could harm and all they ever did harm. Reddit as a whole wasn't harmed until the admin directly interfered and established a particular concept of acceptable and unacceptable content and imposed that site-wide.

That's why I oppose all attempts, including both PV's and yours, to impose some sort of overarching standards. Mods can only harm individual subs - they have no authority over the site as a whole, so they cannot harm the site as a whole. You (and PV) want authority over the site as a whole - you (and PV) want to be above the mods, able to control them. That authority is necessarily broader than the authority of any individual mods, therefore that authority, WHEN it's captured by noxious assholes, can and will be used to do more damage than individual mods could ever do.

Do you think we should just allow censorship on default subs?

I think that "we" need to stop blithely presuming that "we" get to decree what other people are "allowed" to do.

Moderators never harmed "Reddit." They didn't have (and still don't have) that sort of power. They only harmed individual subs - that's the extent of their authority, so it's all they ever could harm and all they ever did harm. Reddit as a whole wasn't harmed until the admin directly interfered and established a particular concept of acceptable and unacceptable content and imposed that site-wide.

I think PV has some point about defaults. They are given an elevated status and therefore should be held to a high standard in terms of free speech and user input into how they are run. If either moderators or admins control the narrative of defaults, they control the narrative of the site in general, and they have an effect on what type of users will eventually stay on voat.

You (and PV) want authority over the site as a whole

I don't intend to act. In fact, most of my propositions are entirely impossible for me to act on. I find the idea of a self-governing online community to be intriguing enough to warrant discussion. Voat's motto is "have your say."

I think your opinion would be essential at /v/voatcongress if you're willing. You offer intelligent criticism.

I think PV has some point about defaults. They are given an elevated status and therefore should be held to a high standard in terms of free speech and user input into how they are run.

I think the much better solution is to do away with defaults and their "elevated status," or, at the very least, change the manner in which they're determined.

All subs should compete on the same level playing field. The good subs (which certainly includes ones that are well-moderated) will be rewarded with subscribers (and potentially with something more or less equivalent to "default" status), while the poor subs (which certainly includes poorly moderated ones) will have fewer subscribers and/or more blockers and absolutely no chance at "default" status. That is as it should be.

I think the whole idea of establishing a sub as a default THEN demanding some particular level of quality in its moderation is exactly backwards.

If "we" desire some particular level of quality in moderation, then "we" already have all the tools "we" need to bring it about - we can subscribe to subs that meet it and avoid and/or block subs that don't. The establishment of defaults skews that process. Yes - it elevates the status of the subs that are made defaults, and that's exactly the problem. If such a concept is to exist at all, it should be a reward for meeting the quality standards the users desire. If a "default" doesn't meet those standards, that doesn't mean that the users should be able to intervene - it means that the sub shouldn't be a "default."
